He progressively reduced his use of the psychotropic drug lithium, at an experimental clinic in Costa Rica. What ensued was a self-exploration into alternative treatments to treat his condition and a journey delving into the root cause of his mental breakdown. The film uses Ross' personal experiences to tell a larger story about medication. evidence: Drummer Gabriel keeps his recent bipolar diagnosis from his bandmates.

title: The Enormity of Life
synopsis: After a failed suicide attempt, a man receives a substantial inheritance from a long lost relative and meets a struggling single mom with an eccentric young daughter. Together they embark on a journey of self discovery and healing.

title: The Flames of Me
synopsis: How do you rebuild your sense of self after being diagnosed with bipolar disorder? Daniel Léger experienced his first manic episode in his early thirties. evidence: Daniel Léger recalls his first manic episode and the bipolar diagnosis that followed.

title: The Flying Scotsman

evidence: Graeme Obree’s mental health struggles are part of the film, and he later described receiving a diagnosis of bipolar disorder.

title: The Ghost and the Whale
synopsis: A man, Joseph, loses his wife at sea, then spirals deep into a world of confusion. The wife's brothers' need revenge! evidence: Joseph Hawthorne is portrayed as a man living with bipolar disorder.

title: The Girl He Met Online
synopsis: A man's relationship with a bipolar woman becomes dangerous.
evidence: Gillian Casey is portrayed as living with bipolar disorder.

title: The God Committee

evidence: Walter Curtis identifies himself as bipolar during an evaluation.

title: The Hero's Journey to the Third Pole
synopsis: Part road movie, part musical, part serious inquiry into the caverns of the mind. evidence: Two people’s experiences of bipolar disorder are the focus of this musical documentary.

title: The Hive
synopsis: As far as they can remember, Marion, Claire and Louise have been living at the pace of their mother Alice’s ups and downs. evidence: Alice’s bipolar disorder shapes her relationship with her daughters.

title: The Holly Kane Experiment
synopsis: An obsessive psychologist attempts to reprogramme her subconscious mind, but when her actions become increasingly uncharacteristic she fears her experiment is dangerously out of control.
evidence: Holly learns that her mother was bipolar during a discussion of her family’s mental health history.

title: The Informant!
synopsis: A rising star at agri-industry giant Archer Daniels Midland (ADM), Mark Whitacre suddenly turns whistleblower. Even as he exposes his company’s multi-national price-fixing conspiracy to the FBI, Whitacre envisions himself being hailed as a hero of the common man and handed a promotion.
evidence: Mark Whitacre’s bipolar diagnosis is part of his story in this biographical film.

title: The Killing of Kenneth Chamberlain
synopsis: Based on the true story of the events that led to the death of Kenneth Chamberlain Sr., an elderly African American veteran with bipolar disorder, who was killed during a conflict with police officers who were dispatched to check on him.
evidence: Kenneth Chamberlain Sr. is portrayed as living with bipolar disorder.

title: The Listener
synopsis: Beth is a helpline volunteer – part of the small army that gets on the phone every night across America, fielding calls from all kinds of people feeling lonely, broken, hopeless. evidence: A caller struggling with bipolar disorder appears briefly in this film’s crisis-line conversations.

title: The Mess
synopsis: As Ellice gets low, her room gets messy - she never sees it coming, but it always happens. There seems to be no way to break out of the endless highs or lows that make up bipolar, or even to pick up her clothes up off the floor.
evidence: Performer Ellice Stevens shares her experience of bipolar disorder in this documentary short.

title: The Next Great American Game
synopsis: Randall Hoyt is an aspiring game designer on the road to publishing his first board game. His wry observations about life, gaming and his own struggles with being bipolar drive this story about what it takes to get a board game published.
evidence: Game designer Randall Hoyt discusses bipolar disorder and creativity in this documentary.

title: The Not So Secret Life of the Manic Depressive: 10 Years On

evidence: The programme revisits people living with bipolar disorder ten years after Stephen Fry’s earlier documentary.

title: The Only Living Boy in New York
synopsis: When a young man learns that his overbearing father is having an affair, he tries to stop it, only to be seduced by the older woman as well.

title: The Other Half
synopsis: A grief-stricken man and a bipolar woman fall in love and attempt to forge a simple life together.
evidence: Emily lives with rapid-cycling bipolar I disorder.

title: The Outrun

evidence: Rona’s father Andrew lives with bipolar disorder and experiences depressive and manic episodes.

title: The Perfect Guy
synopsis: With a fulfilling career and a loving relationship, lobbyist Leah Vaughn seems to have it all. evidence: Robert Adams is called bipolar in a brief exchange that also describes psychosis.

title: The Polar Boy

Breaking the law together with Hanna, Mattias risks everything dear to him, not knowing yet, that Hanna's bold acts are only the symptoms of bipolar disorder. In the moment of jelousy Mattias accidentally commits a crime that could put him behind bars for years. The only escape he sees is to get himself declared irresponsible. In order to achieve that Mattias decides to start faking the illness her gilfriend really has - bipolarity.
evidence: Hanna lives with bipolar disorder, while Mattias only pretends to share her diagnosis.

title: The Queen of Basketball
synopsis: Part of the Almost Famous series. She was arguably the greatest women's basketball player. She won three national trophies; she played in the ’76 Olympics; she was drafted to the NBA. But have you ever heard of Lucy Harris?
evidence: Basketball legend Lusia Harris discusses her bipolar diagnosis in this documentary.

title: The Restless
synopsis: Leila and Damien are deeply in love. Despite his bipolar disorder, he tries to pursue his life with her, knowing he may never be able to offer her what she desires.
evidence: Damien lives with bipolar disorder, a central concern in this family drama.

title: The Road to Ruane

evidence: Billy Ruane’s bipolar disorder is part of this documentary about his life.

title: The Salvation Of The World As We Know It

title: The Scream Queen: Daffney
evidence: Wrestler Daffney’s bipolar disorder is part of this documentary episode about her life.

title: The Scribbler

evidence: Micky Adams's daughter discusses his bipolar disorder.

title: The Ultimate Playlist of Noise
synopsis: After learning he must undergo brain surgery that will render him deaf, Marcus, an audio-obsessed high school senior, decides to seize control of his fate by recording the Ultimate Playlist of Noise — a bucket list of all his favorite sounds.

title: The Versions of My Mind

evidence: Jimena lives with conditions described as schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.

title: The Wind at My Door

evidence: Pierre Goupil’s life with bipolar disorder is the focus of this intimate documentary.

title: The Year Between

Clemence struggles to figure out what it means to heal without driving everyone around her… well, crazy. evidence: Clemence Miller faces a bipolar diagnosis in a story drawn from writer-director Alex Heller’s own experience.

title: This Is My Mother

evidence: Judith Haddad leaves a clinic where she has been receiving treatment for bipolar disorder.

title: Troubled Minds: The Lithium Revolution
synopsis: In a disused hospital pantry in the 1940s, an Australian doctor discovered an astonishing treatment for bi-polar disorder (or manic-depression, as it was then known). It would take 20 years of struggle before lithium treatment was finally accepted, but the scientists and psychiatrists who followed Cade's lead persevered. Their work has meant a chance at stability for hundreds of thousands of people around the world, and lithium remains the benchmark for bi-polar treatment today.
evidence: This documentary traces the history of lithium treatment for bipolar disorder.

title: Trust Me
synopsis: Animated short documentary following a young woman's diagnosis of bipolar: a journey of self-acceptance to challenge everyday stigma. In "Trust Me", a genre-bending short documentary, a young woman uses humour and compassion to share her moving and deeply personal story of coming to terms with her mental health condition. When she starts exhibiting atypical and extreme behaviour, her loved ones trick her into hospitalisation against her will. She is diagnosed with bipolar disorder which starts her challenging journey of self-acceptance, confronting internalised and societal stigma, and learning to trust herself and others again.
evidence: Anne Chataigné lives with bipolar disorder in this hybrid documentary about her experience.

title: Two Lovers
synopsis: A depressed man moves back in with his parents following a recent heartbreak and finds himself with two women.
evidence: Leonard’s mother mentions that he still has a bipolar problem.

title: Two Ways Home

Her return home is turbulent and a rough, unwelcome transition in which Kathy must come to terms with her diagnosis and its implications on her identity, while also realizing that her family was happier when she was gone. Conflict with her family intensifies as she struggles to keep her head above water, putting her self-worth and well-being to the ultimate test.
evidence: Kathy learns she has bipolar II disorder and begins treatment.

title: Type 2

evidence: This short explores bipolar II disorder and its effect on a relationship.

title: Ulbert
evidence: Artist Joe Ulbert’s experience of bipolar disorder is the focus of this film.

evidence: People who report bipolar diagnoses share their experiences in this documentary.

title: Uproot

title: Viplas/Rachana

evidence: Painter Rachana lives with bipolar disorder.

title: Vivien Leigh, autant en emporte le vent

evidence: Vivien Leigh’s bipolarity is a central subject of this documentary portrait.

title: Walking Man

evidence: Mark and Eric Norwine, a father and son, share their experiences of bipolar disorder during their walk across Missouri.

title: We Are Skateboarders: A Mental Health Transformation

As attention grew, Ben’s mental health deteriorated, forcing him to question the meaning of success in life and art. His healing began through therapy, where he confronted trauma, shame, guilt, and complex PTSD linked to the filmmaking experience. The documentary captures his transformation from immense pain toward catharsis, self-love, and compassion. It is a raw and inspiring exploration of resilience, creativity, and mental health.
evidence: Ben Duffy's documentary presents his experience of living with undiagnosed bipolar disorder.

title: We Don't Belong Here
synopsis: A matriarch of a dysfunctional family is pushed to her tipping point by the disappearance of her son.
evidence: Max Green is described as bipolar, while a suggestion that Lily might be bipolar remains tentative.

title: Welcome to Me

evidence: Alice Klieg recounts being diagnosed with bipolar disorder and later rapid-cycling bipolar disorder, before clinicians called her condition borderline personality disorder.

title: What Happened, Miss Simone?
synopsis: The film chronicles Nina Simone's journey from child piano prodigy to iconic musician and passionate activist, told in her own words.
evidence: Nina Simone's daughter reflects on her mother's moods and bipolar disorder.

And how do you break the taboo that still exists on disease pressure?
evidence: Jöran Moerkens discusses living with bipolar disorder in this personal documentary.

title: Wild Cloudberries
synopsis: Bipolar Hilla cannot help but fall in love when she meets bohemian and free-spirited Jemina.
evidence: Hilla lives with bipolar disorder in this short film.

title: Wir für immer
synopsis: Sixteen-year-old Jann shields his mother Lina from the outside world in a system that has been established over the years. evidence: Lina lives with bipolar disorder in this story about a mother and her son.

title: Xabi: A Phantasmagoric Adventure
synopsis: 4 people with psycho-social disability share their stories. evidence: Four people discuss experiences described as bipolar symptoms in this documentary, without assigning a diagnosis to any one participant.

title: You Will Meet a Tall Dark Stranger
synopsis: Two married couples find only trouble and heartache as their complicated lives unfold. evidence: Greg Clemente’s off-screen wife is described as bipolar.

title: Yung Lean: In My Head
synopsis: When a Swedish teen rapper finds a rabid fanbase via the internet, international superstar Yung Lean is born. But as his fame grows, darkness settles in, blurring the line between reality and his own vivid imagination.
evidence: Musician Yung Lean’s struggles with bipolar disorder and drug use are part of this documentary.

title: ZAAD
synopsis: ZAAD tells the autobiographical story of Dries Meddens. After the death of his mother, the care for Dries' bipolar father falls on his plate. Strolling through the family’s film and photo archives, with dramatic and sometimes hilarious finds, Dries tries to find answers. He also consults a psychiatrist. Together the consultations and reviewing of his archival material help Dries look at bipolarity with new eyes.
evidence: Dries Meddens explores his father’s bipolar disorder and his own fear of inheriting it.

evidence: Director Louiselle Noël speaks about receiving a bipolar diagnosis as an adult while the film also introduces children with the condition.

title: 清醒边缘
evidence: Wu Hao lives with bipolar disorder in this documentary.

evidence: Jess is described as having bipolar disorder.

title: Abraxas

evidence: Monty Rushmore is described as having bipolar disorder in this political satire.

evidence: Spalding Gray recounts being told he had bipolar disorder and describes treatment with lithium.

title: Ankahee
synopsis: A femme fatale sinks her claws into the life of a married doctor and his family.
evidence: Kavya is portrayed as living with bipolar disorder.

evidence: Bipolar disorder is one of the conditions represented among the four people in this documentary.

title: Be Here to Love Me
synopsis: Chronicles the fascinating and often turbulent life of Townes Van Zandt.

evidence: Don Bachardy’s older brother Ted is remembered as having bipolar disorder.

evidence: Morgan's grandfather is described as living with bipolar disorder and alcoholism in a brief family conversation.

evidence: Walter Neff mentions bipolar disorder in the family of a woman he nearly married.

title: End of the Road
synopsis: Moments after receiving his graduate diploma, Jacob waits at a train station. The future lies ahead, but life abruptly intervenes. title: Executing the Insane: The Case of Scott Panetti

Panetti was hospitalized, both voluntarily and involuntarily for mental illness fourteen times in six different hospitals before his arrest for capital murder in 1992. Following his conviction, Panetti’s former wife, and daughter of the victims, Sonja Alvarado, filed a petition stating that Panetti never should have been tried for the crimes as he was suffering from paranoid delusions at the time of the killings.
evidence: Scott Panetti’s psychiatric history includes expert testimony describing bipolar disorder.

title: Fallen Angels

Meanwhile a serial killer is targeting members of Jacob's band and their families...
evidence: Ruth is said to have been diagnosed and treated for bipolar disorder.

Will May regain her sanity, restore her normal life and unravel the mystery of her true love? Only time will tell.

title: Hardboiled Egg

title: Hurt

evidence: Sarah’s mother Chris is described as having bipolar disorder, with her worsening condition affecting their family.

evidence: Callie Cain is portrayed as a mother living with bipolar disorder in this custody drama.

evidence: Yuko lives with bipolar disorder, and another character is also described as having bipolar disorder.

evidence: Accounts of the film describe Charlie as having bipolar disorder. The film also uses 'bipolar' figuratively in dialogue.

evidence: A police profile briefly describes a suspect's mother as having bipolar disorder.

evidence: A police brigadier in the ensemble is described as having bipolar disorder.

title: Ma vie en cinémascope
synopsis: 1952, Québec - Alys Robi, vocalist at the top of her popularity and recognized worldwide, was interned in spite of herself, by her father. evidence: This biopic portrays singer Alys Robi as living with bipolar disorder.

title: Manic-depressive illness, manic type
evidence: This archival clinical film shows a patient diagnosed with manic-depressive illness during a manic phase.

title: Music Within

evidence: Arthur Honeyman says he has bipolar disorder in the film.

title: Natural Enemies
synopsis: Paul Steward, editor of a scientific journal, considers his life to be an empty failure. Awake one morning after a sleepless night, he comes to a decision: this evening he will take a rifle and shoot and kill his wife, their three children and then himself.
evidence: Paul’s wife Miriam is portrayed as having bipolar disorder.

title: Neo Ned
synopsis: Like most kids, Ned idolized his father and dreamed of following in his footsteps. Unfortunately, his father was a two-bit crook who spent most of his life in jail. evidence: An unnamed patient identifies bipolar disorder as the reason for their institutionalization.

title: Nightmare Nurse
synopsis: After Brooke and her boyfriend Lance have a car accident, Lance’s leg injury requires him to be bedridden with at-home care. evidence: Nurse Chloe Spade is described as having bipolar disorder during a discussion of her medication.

title: Norman Lear: Just Another Version of You
synopsis: Arguably the most influential creator, writer, and producer in the history of television, Norman Lear brought primetime into step with the times. Using comedy and indelible characters, his legendary 1970s shows such as All In the Family, Maude, Good Times, and The Jeffersons, boldly cracked open dialogue and shifted the national consciousness, injecting enlightened humanism into sociopolitical debates on race, class, creed, and feminism.
evidence: Norman Lear recalls learning that Frances Lear had bipolar disorder during their marriage.

title: On the Edge of Innocence
synopsis: Teenage Zoe Tyler suffers from manic-depression. With a musician father who is never around life seems hard. Zoe eventually lands up in a psychiatric ward for treatment. Fuming, Jake suddenly sees a chance for escape and takes Zoe with him, along with a few other patients. After a trip around the country, Jake and Zoe must face up to their illness and their crime.
evidence: Zoe Tyler is portrayed as having bipolar disorder and receiving psychiatric care.

title: Open Call / Svlíkání
synopsis: A bittersweet summer story about the emotional isolation of two young friends in the closed world of a boarding school in a small spa town. A long-awaited agency arrives in town looking for new faces in the modeling world. A dubious casting call begins, one of the last opportunities to escape the boredom of everyday life. Lenka is determined to get her way, but her plans to break through with her beauty cannot be thwarted by her friend Anička, who no longer wants to stay in Lenka's shadow, her distrustful boyfriend Petr, or the manic-depressive photographer Dan and his assistant Filip. A big game is unfolding in a small space where childhood dreams mix with adult whimsy and hidden desires with hidden hatreds.
evidence: Dan, a supporting photographer, is described as having bipolar disorder.

title: Pollock
synopsis: In August of 1949, Life Magazine ran a banner headline that begged the question: "Jackson Pollock: Is he the greatest living painter in the United States?" The film is a look back into the life of an extraordinary man, a man who has fittingly been called "an artist dedicated to concealment, a celebrity who nobody knew." As he struggled with self-doubt, engaging in a lonely tug-of-war between needing to express himself and wanting to shut the world out, Pollock began a downward spiral.
evidence: Jackson Pollock is portrayed as having bipolar disorder in this biographical film.

title: Princess
synopsis: Princess tells the true story of former cabaret dancer Anna Lappalainen's redemptive struggle with insanity, who checked in to Finland's Kellokoski Psychiatric Hospital in 1945.
evidence: Anna Lappalainen is described as having bipolar disorder and symptoms of schizophrenia.

title: Richard Müller: Nespoznaný
synopsis: For 25 years, Richard Müller has been a key figure in the Czech and Slovak music industry. Despite quitting music once, he returned to the stage while battling untreated manic depression and drug use. The documentary offers an intimate look at his artistic journey and personal struggles, amidst constant fan and tabloid attention. Filmed over three years with over 200 hours of footage, it includes home videos shot by Müller. It follows the tradition of Czech artistic documentaries like Amy and Nick Cave: 20,000 Days on Earth, exploring themes of inspiration and loneliness.
evidence: Singer Richard Müller’s bipolar disorder is central to this documentary.

title: Rocks in My Pockets
synopsis: The personal story of a woman struggling with an inherited illness, as told by Signe Baumane, the Latvian director-animator living in New York City. With humour and courage, the director sets out on a challenging journey to discover her family’s best-kept secret. Featuring five stories about the courageous women in Signe’s family and their battles with madness, visual metaphors, surreal images and director’s narration.
evidence: Signe Baumane explores her family history and a diagnosis later described as bipolar disorder in this animated film.

title: Scala!!! or, The Incredibly Strange Rise and Fall of the World's Wildest Cinema and How It Influenced a Mixed-up Generation of Weirdos and Misfits
synopsis: This feature-length big screen documentary tells the riotous inside story of the infamous sex, drugs and rock 'n' roll repertory cinema which inspired a generation during Britain's turbulent Thatcher years.
evidence: An interviewee recalls that his brother, who died at the Scala cinema, was later described as having bipolar disorder.

title: Scheherazade, Tell Me a Story
synopsis: Heba is a TV presenter interested in broadcasting stories that touch on the everyday secret lives of women and the social injustices they face. Her frank style in broadcasting puts her husband's job and consequently her marriage in jeopardy.
evidence: Amany, one of the guest characters, is described as having bipolar disorder.

title: Screaming Lord Sutch
synopsis: David “Screaming Lord” Sutch (1940-1999) the flamboyantly, bipolar, berserk rock singer, emerging from a coffin, armed with prop knives, axes and skulls, and belting out his song Jack the Ripper. But David Sutch was also the founder of the Official Monster Raving Loony Party and served as its leader from 1983 to 1999, during which time he stood in numerous parliamentary elections.
evidence: The documentary profiles David Sutch, who lived with manic depression.

title: Shadow of Doubt
synopsis: An attorney uncovers a political conspiracy in the brutal killing of a wealthy young woman.

evidence: Dolores Chanal is described as having bipolar disorder in the film.

title: Sing Street
synopsis: A boy growing up in Dublin during the 1980s escapes his strained family life by starting a band to impress the mysterious girl he likes.
evidence: Raphina mentions that her mother has bipolar disorder.

synopsis: Arliss goes to a coffee house to meet Jasmine on a blind date, but she's not quite what she seems.

title: Tammy's Always Dying
synopsis: A daughter's attempt to care for her ornery, ailing mother.
evidence: Tammy describes herself as having bipolar disorder.

synopsis: When Arnie Silverman, a manic-depressive novelist, begins a bout of self-harm and lies to his girlfriend about it, his best friend and sister’s ex-boyfriend unintentionally lead him on a path to a new romance that could potentially solve his problems or send him to rock bottom.
evidence: Novelist Arnie Silverman lives with bipolar disorder in this film.

title: The Boys Next Door
synopsis: Kind-hearted social worker Jack Palmer feels guilty about not spending enough time with his wife due to the pressures of his job taking care of four developmentally disabled men: obsessive-compulsive Norman, bipolar Arnold, childlike Lucien, and schizophrenic Barry. When Jack announces his decision to leave his job, his four charges react quite unexpectedly to the news.
evidence: Arnold Wiggins, one of the group-home residents, is portrayed as having bipolar disorder.

title: The Desperado from Kolsva
synopsis: About Jösta Hagelbäck (1945-2009), Swedish film director, writer, poet, musician, actor etc. A human bipolar mixture of genius and madman. Invited to Hollywood, had an artistic hit with the film "Kejsaren/The Emperor" (1979) at the Berlin Film Festival.
evidence: This documentary profiles artist Jösta Hagelbäck, who is described as having bipolar disorder.

title: The Devil and Daniel Johnston
synopsis: This 2005 documentary film chronicles the life of Daniel Johnston, a manic-depressive genius singer/songwriter/artist, from childhood up to the present, with an emphasis on his mental illness and how it manifested itself in demonic self-obsession.
evidence: Daniel Johnston's bipolar disorder diagnosis and psychiatric care are central to this documentary about his life and music.

title: The Group
synopsis: It's 1933, and eight young women are friends and members of the upper-class group at a private girl's school, about to graduate and start their own lives. evidence: Polly’s father Henry Andrews is portrayed as having bipolar disorder.

title: The Hudsucker Proxy
synopsis: A naive business graduate is installed as president of a manufacturing company as part of a stock scam.
evidence: Norville Barnes is labelled as having bipolar disorder in a brief clinical exchange.

title: The Initiated

In the saga of Frank Molina, which uses the books Lady Massacre, La melancolia de los feos, El diario del fin del mundo and Akelarre, the story of an alcoholic private investigator who unmasks sinister plots within the underworld of Bogotá is told.
evidence: Frank Molina is portrayed as living with bipolar disorder.

title: The Last Days of Disco
synopsis: Two young women and their friends spend spare time at an exclusive nightclub in 1980s New York.
evidence: Josh’s friends connect his religious mania to bipolar disorder, and he later describes depression and lithium treatment.

title: The Man on the Eiffel Tower
synopsis: A down-and-out student is hired to kill a wealthy woman. When someone else is suspected of the crime, the student taunts police until they realize that they may have to wrong man.
evidence: Johann Radek is portrayed as having bipolar disorder.

title: The other city
synopsis: In 2007 Livi, a photography student, moves into an empty building in downtown Haifa. The joint work thrives and their voice is heard across the distance, but cracks begin to show, the gallery closes and they disperse. For 12 years, Livi follows their journey to fulfill their dreams as they face the reality of livelihood difficulties, manic depression and alcoholism, unfolding both intimately and lovingly, revealing the story of five friends and their maturing process.
evidence: Five friends’ lives are followed over twelve years as they contend with problems including bipolar disorder.

title: The Silence of the Lambs
synopsis: Clarice Starling is a top student at the FBI's training academy.  Jack Crawford wants Clarice to interview Dr. Hannibal Lecter, a brilliant psychiatrist who is also a violent psychopath, serving life behind bars for various acts of murder and cannibalism.  Crawford believes that Lecter may have insight into a case and that Starling, as an attractive young woman, may be just the bait to draw him out.
evidence: Hannibal Lecter briefly describes his former patient Benjamin Raspail as having bipolar disorder.

title: The World of Z

evidence: Artist Zbigniew Fiks lives with bipolar disorder in this documentary portrait.

title: This Much is True
synopsis: Lewis Riley, a writer in the inner-city suburbs of Sydney, socialises with a host of colourful characters at a dingy 150-year-old pub, The Rising Sun. There’s a rogue chemist, a once famous drag queen, a violent debt collector, a con man, a manic depressive, and a fixer. Each has an outrageous, compelling and often criminal story to tell.
evidence: A customer in this filmed stage production is described as having bipolar disorder.

title: Three Identical Strangers

evidence: Eddy Galland’s former wife recalls that doctors eventually described his condition as bipolar disorder.

title: Tree of Hands
synopsis: A woman is attempting to cope with her son's tragic death when her mother arrives on an ill-timed visit with her own remedies.
evidence: Marsha, Benet’s mother, has bipolar disorder and psychotic episodes.

title: Tyson

TYSON alternates between the controversial boxer addressing the camera and shots of the champion's fights to create an arresting picture of the man.
evidence: Mike Tyson's earlier medical evaluation recorded a diagnosis of bipolar disorder and lithium treatment, part of the mental health history surrounding this documentary.

title: Waiting for Bojangles
synopsis: A boy and his eccentric parents leave their home in Paris for a country house in Spain. As the mother descends deeper into her own mind, it's up to the boy and his father to keep her safe and happy.
evidence: Camille's mental health is central to this film, which identifies her as having bipolar disorder.

title: Weirdo: The Story of Five Eight
synopsis: After being institutionalized for schizophrenia and manic-depression in his early 20s, Mike Mantione turned to songwriting as a way of dealing with his demons. For 30 years, loud guitars have kept those demons at bay.
evidence: Mike Mantione’s symptoms associated with bipolar disorder and psychiatric care are part of this documentary about the band Five Eight.

title: Went to Coney Island on a Mission from God... Be Back by Five

evidence: Richie is portrayed as living with bipolar disorder.

title: Grizzly Man
synopsis: Follows the story of "Grizzly Man" Timothy Treadwell and what the thirteen summers in a National Park in Alaska were like in his attempt to protect the grizzly bears. The film is full of unique images and a look into the spirit of a man who sacrificed himself for nature.
evidence: Timothy Treadwell’s life has been interpreted through a posthumous bipolar attribution, but the documentary does not establish a diagnosis.

title: Game of Throws: Inside Darts
evidence: Darts player James Wade discusses his bipolar diagnosis in the series.

title: Aaron Carter: The Little Prince of Pop
synopsis: Famous by age 9, struggling by age 20 and dead at ripe age of 34, this documentary dives deep into the life of pop singer Aaron Carter. Just a few years after his rise to fame, Carter began a cycle of mental health struggles, experienced family turmoil, and grappled with addiction ― culminating in his untimely death in November 2022.
evidence: Aaron Carter publicly said he had been diagnosed with bipolar disorder.

title: Abraham and Mary Lincoln: A House Divided
evidence: Mary Todd Lincoln’s mental health and institutionalization feature in this documentary. Later suggestions that she had bipolar disorder remain disputed.

title: Aby Warburg: Metamorphosis and Memory
synopsis: Aby Warburg was an original and influential art historian, whose range was cross cultural, seeking the afterlife of antiquity.
evidence: Aby Warburg’s depression and psychiatric hospitalization are part of this documentary. Historical records give conflicting diagnoses, including bipolar disorder.

title: Ailey
synopsis: Alvin Ailey was a visionary artist who found salvation through dance. Told in his own words and through the creation of a dance inspired by his life, this immersive portrait follows a man who, when confronted by a world that refused to embrace him, determined to build one that would.
evidence: A brief sequence depicts Alvin Ailey’s bipolar state, according to the film’s director. An archival chronology also records his diagnosis.

title: Amando a Maradona
synopsis: What do they have in common a boy playing in a field of Villa Fiorito and the owner of a bar in Naples? What do they have in common 500 people celebrating Christmas on October 30 and 25 football fans showing their tattoos? They are all loving Maradona.
evidence: A clinician attributed bipolar disorder to Diego Maradona in 2026, long after this documentary was made.

title: American Nightmare
evidence: A reporter in the series says Matthew Muller told detectives he was bipolar.

title: Armed With Words & Wings
evidence: Poet Michael Strunge’s bipolar disorder is part of this documentary about his life and work.

title: Battle Mountain: Graeme Obree's Story

Will his ageing body and fragile psyche cope with the pressure he will find on Nevada's State Route 305?
evidence: Graeme Obree’s depression and suicide attempts are covered in the film. He later spoke publicly about a bipolar diagnosis.

title: Being Gail Porter
evidence: Gail Porter describes receiving conflicting diagnoses, including bipolar I and bipolar II, in this personal documentary. She says she does not know which label applies.

evidence: Laura Delano discusses having taken medication for a bipolar diagnosis that she later left behind. The film also features other people diagnosed with bipolar disorder.

title: Crazywise
synopsis: Western culture treats mental disorders primarily through biomedical psychiatry, but filmmakers Phil Borges and Kevin Tomlinson reveal a growing movement of professionals and survivors who are forging alternative treatments that focus on recovery and turning mental “illness” into a positive transformative experience.
evidence: Laura Delano appears in this film about psychological crises. She has spoken about receiving a bipolar diagnosis at 14 and later rejecting psychiatric labels.

title: Crime Scene: The Vanishing at the Cecil Hotel
evidence: Elisa Lam’s bipolar diagnosis, medication and her own posts are discussed in the series. Its final episode also recounts the coroner’s view that the condition contributed to her death.

title: Dangerous Edge: A Life of Graham Greene
synopsis: The documentary uses Graham Greene's own words from his books and recordings, as well as photographs and clips from his many films, to reveal the fascinating life of one of the great writers of the twentieth century.
evidence: Graham Greene's life and writing are viewed through a retrospective interpretation of bipolar disorder in this documentary.

title: Death Row Stories: Nathan Dunlap
evidence: Nathan Dunlap’s reported bipolar diagnosis, lithium treatment and family history are discussed in this episode. It presents competing views about the condition’s relevance to his case.

title: Demi Lovato: Simply Complicated
synopsis: A personal and intimate look into Demi Lovato's life as not only a regular 25 year old, but also one of the biggest pop stars in the world.
evidence: Demi Lovato recounts an earlier bipolar diagnosis in this documentary. Lovato later said the diagnosis was inaccurate.

title: Diagnonsense
synopsis: A self-reflexive meta-documentary. Filmmaker Ane-Martha Tamnes Hansgard was diagnosed with multiple mental disorders over fifteen years and was prescribed a staggering number of psychotropic medications.
evidence: Laura Delano, who has questioned a bipolar diagnosis she received as a teenager, appears in this film about psychiatric labels.

title: Diego Maradona
synopsis: Constructed from over 500 hours of never-before-seen footage, this documentary centers on the personal life and career of the controversial football player Diego Maradona who played for SSC Napoli and Argentina in the 1980s.
evidence: A clinician attributed bipolar disorder to Diego Maradona in 2026, seven years after this documentary’s release.

title: DMX: Don’t Try to Understand
synopsis: A focus on a year in the life of rapper Earl “DMX” Simmons as he is released from prison in early 2019 and attempts to rebuild his career in the music industry and reconnect with family and fans.
evidence: DMX publicly said he had bipolar disorder. This documentary covers his addiction and family life.

title: Dreams with Sharp Teeth
synopsis: The documentary story of Harlan Ellison
evidence: A friend attributed bipolar disorder to Harlan Ellison.

title: Edvard Munch
synopsis: Edvard Munch's childhood is overshadowed by death: he suffers the loss of his sister and mother, while enduring serious illness himself, almost dying. evidence: Edvard Munch has sometimes been retrospectively described as bipolar, an attribution disputed by psychiatric scholarship.

title: F. Scott Fitzgerald and “The Last of the Belles”
synopsis: A semi-fictional account of how writer F. Scott Fitzgerald met his wife while he was in the army and stationed in Alabama in 1919.
evidence: Some later writers have speculated that F. Scott Fitzgerald had bipolar disorder.

evidence: Paul Gascoigne’s bipolar label has been publicly disputed, including by Gascoigne himself. This documentary covers his football career and alcohol use.

title: Gene Tierney: A Forgotten Star
evidence: Gene Tierney’s years of mental illness are part of this documentary. A historical account reports a bipolar diagnosis and hospitalization.

evidence: Justin Furstenfeld’s depression and reported bipolar disorder are among the mental health experiences covered in this documentary. Public accounts of his exact diagnosis conflict.

evidence: Dee Dee Ramone was later reported to have been diagnosed with bipolar disorder.

evidence: Randy Meisner was reported to have received a bipolar diagnosis in 2015, after this Eagles documentary was released.
